name: Artificial Analysis
metricFocus: Intelligence Index, Real API $/Task & First-Token Speed
whatItMeasures: Runs identical standardized reasoning, coding, and knowledge suites across live commercial & open-weight endpoints while clocking real API latency (time to first token), throughput (tokens/sec), and exact dollar cost per task.
whyTrustIt: No self-reported vendor numbers—Artificial Analysis queries live production APIs continuously so you see true speed and pricing trade-offs alongside capability.
knownBlindSpot: Synthetic composite scores don't capture subtle brand voice, long-horizon agent tool failures, or private enterprise RAG accuracy.
bestForTasks: Comparing cost-per-task, speed vs. IQ trade-offs, and 2-person team split economics.

name: SWE-bench Verified
whatItMeasures: Gives AI models real, unresolved GitHub issues from major open-source Python repositories and grades them strictly on whether their generated code patch passes the repository's real unit test suite.
whyTrustIt: You can't bluff a passing test suite. It mirrors genuine software engineering debugging rather than toy LeetCode puzzles.
knownBlindSpot: Skews heavily toward Python backend repos; less coverage of frontend CSS/UI polish, DevOps, or greenfield system architecture.
bestForTasks: Debugging gnarly codebases, legacy refactoring, and automated unit test generation.

name: LMArena (Chatbot Arena)
whatItMeasures: Millions of everyday users type real prompts, see two anonymous model responses side-by-side, and vote on which answer actually helped them more—producing chess-style Elo rankings.
whyTrustIt: Hard to game because prompts are open-ended and voters don't know which lab generated which reply until after voting.
knownBlindSpot: Humans can be charmed by confident formatting, verbosity, or polite tone—even when an answer hides a subtle factual or legal mistake.
bestForTasks: Everyday writing, marketing copy, teaching clarity, polite emails, and tone warmth.

name: LiveBench
whatItMeasures: Releases brand-new questions every month pulled from recent arXiv papers, news, math competitions, and coding challenges—with objective automated grading (no LLM judge bias).
whyTrustIt: Eliminates 'test set memorization' (contamination) because models couldn't possibly have seen this month's fresh problems during training.
knownBlindSpot: Focuses on hard objective puzzles; doesn't evaluate creative storytelling, audio/video perception, or empathetic human coaching.
bestForTasks: High-stakes logic, financial/legal reasoning checks, and verifying genuine reasoning gains.

name: MMMU & MMMU-Pro
whatItMeasures: Tests whether a model truly understands visual information—engineering schematics, medical scans, sheet music, financial charts, and UI screenshots—across 30 expert disciplines.
whyTrustIt: MMMU-Pro strips out questions that can be guessed from text alone, proving whether the model genuinely sees pixels vs. guessing.
knownBlindSpot: Primarily evaluates static images and structured visual frames; long-form continuous video and live voice prosody need additional media tests.
bestForTasks: UI screenshot debugging, chart/PDF extraction, lecture videos, and photo diagnostics.

name: Stanford HELM
organization: Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models
whatItMeasures: Evaluates models across seven dimensions simultaneously—accuracy, calibration (knowing when it's unsure), robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, and efficiency—across legal, medical, and enterprise domains.
whyTrustIt: Peer-reviewed academic rigor that exposes hidden failure modes like overconfidence and sycophancy that leaderboard headlines hide.
knownBlindSpot: Academic evaluation cycles update slightly slower than day-one frontier API drops.
bestForTasks: Legal/compliance audits, citation fact-checking, enterprise RAG, and high-stakes honesty.

name: Open LLM Leaderboard
whatItMeasures: Evaluates downloadable open-weight models (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral) under identical open harness settings across MMLU-Pro, GPQA, MATH, MuSR, and IFEval instruction following.
whyTrustIt: 100% open, reproducible test harness—vital for teams deciding whether a self-hosted open-weight model can replace a proprietary API.
knownBlindSpot: Covers open-weight checkpoints only; closed proprietary APIs (Claude, GPT, Gemini) are tracked separately.
bestForTasks: Choosing private, self-hosted, or VPC-deployed open-weight models (Llama 4, Qwen 3, DeepSeek, Mistral).

name: Epoch AI Benchmarks
whatItMeasures: Maintains independent PhD-level scientific reasoning (GPQA Diamond), research-grade mathematics (FrontierMath), and longitudinal cost/compute trend datasets across major AI labs.
whyTrustIt: Respected non-profit research institute focused on clean methodology, uncontaminated expert-authored math, and transparent frontier trend analysis.
knownBlindSpot: Ultra-hard research benchmarks mostly separate the top Principal tier and don't tell you which 15¢ Associate writes the warmest email.
bestForTasks: Validating Principal-tier research, PhD paper synthesis, and deep technical breakthroughs.
